newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria party says neutrality must be put to vote.
newsitem.headline: Austria party says neutrality must be put to vote.

text.p: Austria's governing Social Democrats said on Wednesday it remained opposed to joining a military alliance but any change to the country's neutrality had to be decided in a referendum.

Heinz Fischer, parliamentary Speaker of the dominant Social Democratic Party (SPOE), said it was fundamentally against changes to Austria's 41-year neutrality, but if it was to be called into question, it had to be put to a vote.
"The SPOe does not think it is sensible to exchange the country's neutrality for a military alliance," Fischer said in an interview with Die Presse newspaper.
Austria could contribute much more to common European security as a neutral country than a "dwarf at the tailend of NATO", he said.

The SPOe and conservative People's Party (OeVP) coalition has long been divided over whether Austria should ditch its neutral status and become a member of the 16-nation Atlantic alliance or the Western European Union (WEU), the future defence arm of the European Union.
Austria obtained observer status at the WEU after joining the European Union in January last year.
The conservatives have over the past 18 months increasingly backed modifying or ending neutrality, while the far-right Freedom Party has openly called for NATO membership.
But the Social Democrat position appears to have the backing of the majority of Austrians with a recent poll showing only 23 percent of voters in favour of joining NATO.
Austria, perched on the former Cold War border between the feuding Eastern and Western blocs, has been neutral since 1955, when it drew up its post-World War Two constitution.

The Soviet Union, which occupied Austria after the war with allies Britain, France and the United States, demanded Austria enshrine neutrality as a central pillar of its national charter before it agreed to withdraw its troops.

Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said during an official visit to Vienna last Friday that Moscow hoped Austria would remain neutral but any change was now a decision solely for the Austrian people.
